claim: Taman Negara was gazetted in 1938-39 (originally King George V National Park), spans 4,343 km2 across three states, and sits on UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list.
quote: Park gazetted 1938-39 (originally King George V National Park), 4,343 km2 across three states, on UNESCO tentative list.

claim: Taman Negara's rainforest is around 130 million years old, far older than the Amazon (~55 million years).
quote: Taman Negara is ~130 million years old, far older than the Amazon (~55M years).

claim: Taman Negara is on UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list, not yet inscribed — it is not a World Heritage Site.
quote: Taman Negara is on UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list, not yet inscribed.

claim: Mutiara Taman Negara is the only resort inside the national-park boundary — ~87 Malay-style wooden chalets overlooking the Tembeling and Tahan rivers, reached only by boat.
quote: The Only Resort Inside The National Park Boundary ... overlooking the Tembeling and Tahan rivers ... 87-unit accommodations

claim: The best time to visit Taman Negara is March-September, with May-August the driest high season.
quote: aim for the dry months between March and August... May to August is the driest period and therefore high season

claim: The Nov-Feb monsoon brings heavy rain, tricky river crossings and more leeches, and many Kuala Tahan businesses close.
quote: Heavy rain from the monsoon season hits Taman Negara from November to February, making jungle trekking and river crossings tricky

claim: The canopy walkway has been closed since 18 September 2024 until further notice, for maintenance by the Wildlife Department.
quote: Canopy walk will be closed from 18th Sep 2024 until further notice for maintenance by the Wildlife Department

claim: The new Seberang Ara canopy walkway is reported as set to reopen in March 2026, though no firm date is confirmed.
quote: Taman Negara's Seberang Ara canopy walkway to reopen in March next year

claim: Gua Telinga cave is temporarily closed to entry after a rock collapse; the trail to it is still walkable.
quote: temporarily closed for entry due to cave-structure safety (rock collapse); trail still walkable

claim: EUR/MYR traded around 4.6-4.7 in early June 2026, the rate used for conversions here.
quote: the exchange rate of Euro to Malaysian ringgits has fluctuated between a high of 4.70355 on 08-06-2026 and a low of 4.60772 on 02-06-2026

claim: The KL bus+boat combo to Kuala Tahan registers around noon, the longboat departs Kuala Tembeling at 13:00 and arrives ~16:00 (2.5-3hr cruise), for roughly RM140-150.
quote: boats departing at 1300 hours and arriving at Kuala Tahan at 1600 hours... the scenic jungle river cruise takes around 2.5-3 hours

claim: The Kuala Tembeling longboat is afternoon-only (departs ~13:00-13:30); the morning boat was cancelled in 2014, and a KL shuttle bus to Kuala Tahan departs ~08:30.
quote: 1PM - 1.30PM departure... Morning boat had been cancelled in year 2014

claim: The Cameron Highlands to Taman Negara minivan + river-boat combo takes about 5-6 hours including the Jerantut stop and the longboat to Kuala Tahan.
quote: The total travel time is around 5-6 hours, including the minivan transfer from Cameron Highlands, a short stop in Jerantut, and the river boat ride to Kuala Tahan

claim: The Taman Negara to Kuala Besut jetty minivan (gateway to the Perhentian Islands) is RM130 (RM150 from 1 Apr 2026), departing Kuala Tahan 08:00 and arriving ~16:30.
quote: RM 130.00... RM 150.00 (effective April 1, 2026)... Departure: 8:00 AM from Kuala Tahan... Arrival: 4:30 PM at Kuala Besut Jetty

claim: Park entry permits cost RM1 plus a RM5 photography licence; floating-restaurant meals run about RM20 with a drink and cash is preferred.
quote: Park entry permits cost RM1 per permit and RM5 per photography license... Meals on the floating restaurants cost around RM20 for a meal and drink

claim: Kuala Tahan has about half a dozen floating raft restaurants (plus Mutiara's restaurant); all the rafts are dry — no alcohol — and a lunch with drinks runs ~RM35.
quote: floating raft houses on the river... all rafts are dry (no alcohol)... lunch washed down with some drinks costing around 35 RM

claim: Join-tour activity prices: night river cruise from RM65, night jungle walk from RM40, day tour from RM150.
quote: Night River Cruise (Join Tour) From 65 ... Night Jungle Walk (Join Tour) From 40

claim: The rapid-shooting + Orang Asli village day combo costs RM150 (no lunch) or RM170 (with lunch), permit RM5.
quote: Day trip packages are available for RM150 (without lunch) or RM170 (with lunch), and permits are RM5 per person

claim: Bukit Teresek is a self-guided 1.7km hike from HQ to a panoramic viewpoint; wildlife hides (bumbun) sit from 15 minutes to 11km out.
quote: Bukit Teresek ... Only 1.7 km from headquarters; second section is steep. Panoramic views

claim: Lata Berkoh is reached by a ~1hr wooden boat up Sungai Tahan (or an 8.5km trek) and offers scenic cascades and swimming.
quote: Lata Berkoh reached by ~1hr wooden boat up Sungai Tahan or an 8.5km jungle trek; scenic cascades and swimming

claim: Dusk and night safaris near Lubok Simpon and Kumbang Hide are the prime chance to spot shy mammals like tapir.
quote: Dusk/night safaris near Lubok Simpon and Kumbang Hide are prime for spotting shy mammals like tapirs

claim: Guides hire Batek men to demonstrate blowpipe and fire-making, and tourists arriving with junk food and folded banknotes create dependency — the central ethics caution for the village visit.
quote: Visitors arrive with bags of rice, bread, junk food, biscuits, and even plastic toys, followed by guides pressing folded banknotes into their palms. This creates dependency.

claim: The Bukit Teresek trail is excellent for hornbills, especially during the April-August fruiting season.
quote: The Bukit Teresek trail is excellent for hornbills, especially during the April to August fruiting season

claim: The 'Jungle Railway' runs Gemas to Tumpat on single metre-gauge track through the interior, earning its nickname.
quote: runs between Gemas in Negeri Sembilan and Tumpat in Kelantan... through deep jungle, thus earning the nickname Jungle Railway.

claim: Kuala Lipis was Pahang's capital from 1898 to 1955, grown rich on gold and timber, then declined when the capital moved.
quote: Kuala Lipis was the capital of Pahang from 1898 to 1955... the state capital was shifted to Kuantan, and Kuala Lipis fell into decline.
